section_summary: This concluding section of file 894.021 covers the organization, personnel, and institutional restructuring of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Service from late 1937 through December 1939. Key items include a comprehensive December 1937 roster of Foreign Office officials and diplomatic/consular posts worldwide, detailed reports on bureaucratic and military pressures to reorganize the ministry and subordinate China policy to new continental administrative organs, and the promulgation of Imperial Ordinances Nos. 465 and 466 introducing outside research specialists and dedicated press attachés. The section concludes with diplomatic exchanges in December 1939 conveying personal greetings between President Roosevelt and Foreign Minister Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck regarding the declining authority of the Japanese Foreign Office compared to the military ministries.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference (793.94112/152): with the War and Navy Ministries at the front, the Foreign Office can only repeat what military authorities authorize.
subfiles.title: Authority of Japanese Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a telegram regarding holiday office closures and skeleton staffing at the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Tokyo Telegram No. 684: government offices close January 1-6, but a skeleton staff stayed on duty at the Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Holiday Duty at Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet summarizing a telegram regarding Foreign Minister Hirota's conversation with the British Ambassador Sir Robert Craigie.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Tokyo telegram on Hirota's conversation with British Ambassador Craigie, with Grew's comments on Japanese attitudes toward Britain.
subfiles.title: Conversation of Hirota with Craigie

subfiles.about: Despatch and translated directory listing all officials of the Japanese Foreign Office and diplomatic and consular establishments abroad as of December 1, 1937.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Despatch No. 2867 transmitting an extensive English translation of the official Japanese Foreign Service list as of December 1, 1937. The roster enumerates leadership and section personnel in Tokyo (Secretariat, Bureaus of Eastern Asiatic, European and Asiatic, American, Commercial, Treaties, Information, Cultural Enterprises, and Investigation, as well as the Cultural Enterprises Investigation Committee), followed by ambassadors, ministers, secretaries, attachés, and consuls across all Japanese embassies, legations, and consulates globally.
subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Service List (December 1, 1937)

subfiles.about: State Department digest and Tokyo despatch analyzing Japanese plans to reorganize the Foreign Office and coordinate continental China policy.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Despatch No. 2938 (accompanied by a Division of Far Eastern Affairs summary memorandum by Joseph W. Ballantine dated June 6, 1938) reporting on committee proposals to drastically reorganize the Foreign Office. The proposals envisage converting the East Asia Bureau and Information Section into quasi-independent organs under the Foreign Minister, redistributing regional work into four bureaus, and renaming the department the Ministry of Foreign Policy. Grew examines the broader shift from traditional liberal professional diplomats toward a more nationalistic, military-dominated foreign policy apparatus.
subfiles.title: Japan's China Policy and Proposed Reorganization of the Japanese Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and extracted pages from a Tokyo political report discussing plans for China administrative organs and Foreign Office reform.
subfiles.summary: Political Report No. 124: competing plans for administering China affairs, the Cabinet's March 15 decision for a China Economic Affairs Bureau, and a ten-point Foreign Office reform.
subfiles.title: Administrative Decisions and Proposed Reorganization

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding procedures for preparing Japanese Foreign Office budget appropriation bills.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 2930 on the procedure for preparing the Japanese Foreign Office's appropriation bills.
subfiles.title: Preparation of Appropriation Bills for Japanese Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning Foreign Minister Ugaki's meetings with the British Ambassador regarding foreign interests in China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 572: Ugaki scheduled an August 31 interview with Craigie on foreign interests in China.
subfiles.title: Foreign Minister's Conference with British Ambassador

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet reporting press criticism of Foreign Minister Ugaki and expected diplomatic reassignments under the Anti-Comintern Pact.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 589: ultranationalist papers attack Ugaki for delaying diplomatic changes to strengthen the Anti-Comintern Pact; Kurusu may become Vice Minister.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Representation and the Anti-Comintern Pact

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet and extracted report summarizing senior Japanese diplomatic and consular appointments announced in October 1938.
subfiles.summary: Political Report No. 131 extract: October 1938 appointments, including Oshima as Ambassador to Germany (first Army officer ambassador), Horinouchi to Washington, Togo to Moscow and Shigemitsu to London.
subfiles.title: Foreign Service Changes (October 1938)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording the assignment of Shinichi Chiba to head the Foreign Affairs Department of the Taiwan Government General.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Taihoku report: Shinichi Chiba arrived April 7, 1939 as Chief of Foreign Affairs of the Taiwan Government General.
subfiles.title: Arrival of Shinichi Chiba at Taiwan Government General

subfiles.about: Despatch with translated Imperial Ordinances authorizing outside research specialists in the Foreign Office and information attachés abroad.
subfiles.doc_type: Despatch with enclosures and State Department memoranda
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Despatch No. 4040 from Chargé d'Affaires Eugene H. Dooman (prefaced by internal State Department routing notes by Stanley K. Hornbeck and a FE Division digest) transmitting translations of Imperial Ordinances Nos. 465 and 466 of July 11, 1939. Ordinance 465 permits appointment of specialized research experts from business and academic circles into a revamped Foreign Office policy research organ, circumventing Privy Council objections. Ordinance 466 authorizes Sonin-rank press attachés drawn from journalism to conduct propaganda and information operations at embassies and consulates abroad, posing new diplomatic and legal questions for democratic host countries.
subfiles.title: Administrative Changes in the Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum and diplomatic correspondence transmitting personal greetings between President Roosevelt and Foreign Minister Admiral Nomura.
subfiles.doc_type: Memorandum, diplomatic notes, and official letters
subfiles.from: Kensuke Horinouchi, Sumner Welles, and H. Charles Spruks
subfiles.summary: A dossier comprising an internal State Department memorandum by H. Charles Spruks, a personal note from Japanese Ambassador Kensuke Horinouchi to Secretary Cordell Hull, a transmittal letter to Presidential Secretary Brigadier General Edwin M. Watson, and Sumner Welles's acknowledgment to Horinouchi. The exchange conveys reciprocal good wishes between President Roosevelt and Japanese Foreign Minister Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura stemming from their prior acquaintance when Nomura was Naval Attaché in Washington.
subfiles.title: Exchange of Greetings between President Roosevelt and Foreign Minister Nomura
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, General Edwin M. Watson, and Kensuke Horinouchi
